title: Demo Discovery Questions Bank (Aligned to Talk Track) — v1
body:
Purpose
- A pick-list of discovery questions to tailor the Redwood Inference demo live.
- Designed to map directly to the standard talk track modules:
  1) Core API (chat/streaming/structured output/tool calling)
  2) Production economics (batching/caching + token-level cost)
  3) Reliability (fallback routing / graceful degradation)
  4) Observability (Console cost/latency/errors, tracing, rollouts)
  5) Enterprise/security (SSO/RBAC/audit logs/retention, VPC/Private story)

How to use (quick guidance)
- Ask 2–3 questions max per section; don’t turn the demo into an interview.
- Prefer specific numbers + examples (“what’s your P95 today?”) over generalities (“is latency important?”).
- When they give an answer, confirm what you heard and pivot to the matching demo module.
- Capture in notes: workload type, latency/throughput goals, constraints (data/regulatory), current stack, decision process + timeline.

0) 30-second opener (set context + permission)
- “To make this useful, can I ask 2–3 quick questions about your use case and success criteria? Then we’ll tailor what we show live.”
- “Who’s on the call today—are you evaluating day-to-day integration, or more platform/security readiness?”

1) Primary use case + workload shape (choose your path)
Goal: identify the ‘happy path’ scenario to demo first.

Core questions (ask 2–4)
- “What’s the user-facing feature you’re building with LLMs? (support agent, search, coding assist, internal ops, etc.)”
- “What’s the request type mix: chat generation vs embeddings vs reranking? Rough % breakdown?”
- “What’s the typical prompt/context size today (or expected)? Any long-context requirements?”
- “How many requests per second at peak? And how bursty is it (steady vs spiky)?”
- “What’s ‘good enough’ latency for your end users? (P50/P95 targets if you have them.)”
- “Are responses streamed to the UI, or do you wait for the full completion?”

Follow-ups to route to modules
- If they mention UI/chat: “Do you need deterministic formatting (JSON) or function calls to hit downstream systems?” → Core API (structured output + tool calling)
- If they mention search: “Do you care more about embedding throughput/cost or ranking quality?” → Embeddings/rerank + economics + observability
- If they mention internal batch jobs: “Is throughput or $/token the priority? What’s your acceptable completion window?” → Production economics

2) Current approach + pain (why now)
Goal: surface the pain Redwood solves (latency, cost, reliability, operational overhead).

Core questions
- “What are you using today for inference? (vendor API, self-hosted, cloud endpoints, mix)”
- “What’s working well—and what is painful?”
- “Have you had incidents tied to inference (capacity, rate limits, model changes, quality regressions)?”
- “How do you roll out model changes today? Who owns regressions?”

Probe for specific failure modes (maps to our demo resilience story)
- “Have you ever been throttled (429s) at the worst time?”
- “Any ‘noisy neighbor’ concerns or unpredictable throughput?”
- “Do model updates ever change behavior in ways that break prompts/tools?”
- “If your primary model/region is unavailable, what happens today?”

3) Integration needs (Core API module)
Goal: decide which live API features to emphasize (SDKs, streaming, tools, JSON).

Questions
- “Which language(s) do you need supported first—Python, TypeScript, both?”
- “Do you need OpenAI-compatible endpoints, native SDK, or both?”
- “Do you have tool calling / function calling requirements? What systems would you call?”
- “Do you need structured JSON outputs for downstream parsing? Any schema constraints?”
- “What does retry logic look like in your app today? Do you have idempotency needs?”
- “Do you need per-route quotas or project-level keys for teams/environments (dev/stage/prod)?”

Nice-to-have qualifiers (only if relevant)
- “Any multi-tenant constraints (end-customer isolation)?”
- “Do you need request/response logging? If yes, what do you have to redact?”

4) Production economics (batching/caching + unit cost)
Goal: identify whether cost, latency, or predictability is the priority; tee up token-level breakdown and levers.

Questions
- “What’s the #1 priority: lowest latency, lowest cost, or predictable performance under load?”
- “Do you have a unit economics target? (e.g., $ per conversation / $ per ticket / margin constraints)”
- “Where are costs coming from today—long prompts, high output tokens, retries, or poor batching?”
- “Do you have repeated prefixes (system prompts, templates, RAG boilerplate) that could benefit from caching?”
- “Are you okay trading a bit of latency to reduce cost (batching), or do you need strict latency SLOs?”

Concrete prompts to quantify
- “Average input tokens and output tokens per request?”
- “Peak vs average QPS? Any seasonal spikes?”

Pivot lines (how to transition into the demo)
- “Given you care about X, we’ll show you the exact levers for X—batching/caching knobs and token-level cost + latency breakdown.”

5) Reliability + routing (fallback/graceful degradation module)
Goal: confirm what “reliability” means to them and whether fallback policies matter.

Questions
- “What uptime/availability do you need for the LLM feature? Is it mission-critical or ‘nice-to-have’?”
- “What’s the acceptable degraded mode? (slower responses, cheaper model, smaller context, partial feature off)”
- “If the primary model is saturated, do you prefer to queue, shed load, or fail over to a compatible variant?”
- “Are there region constraints (EU-only, US-only) that affect fallback options?”
- “Do you need per-customer routing (tiered SLAs)?”

Signals to listen for
- “We can’t go down” / “this drives revenue” → emphasize fallback routing + capacity controls + runbooks
- “We can degrade safely” → emphasize policy-based graceful degradation story

6) Observability + operations (Console module)
Goal: identify which Console views to show (cost/latency/errors, traces, rollouts, evals).

Questions
- “Who debugs inference issues today—app team, ML platform, SRE?”
- “When something’s slow, what do you want to see first: model latency breakdown, queueing, tokens, region, errors?”
- “Do you need per-route/model dashboards for different product surfaces?”
- “Do you have tracing today (OpenTelemetry, Datadog, etc.)? Do you need correlation IDs?”
- “How do you catch quality regressions—manual spot checks, eval suites, user feedback?”

Rollouts + versioning prompts
- “How often do you change prompts/models? Do you need canary/A-B or gradual rollouts?”
- “Would you like the ability to pin model versions per environment?”

7) Deployment mode + security posture (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
Goal: decide whether to run the ‘enterprise narrative’ early or keep it as a module for Q&A.

Fast qualifier (ask early if the call has security/IT people)
- “Are you open to a hosted API, or do you require VPC/private deployment from day one?”

Hosted vs Dedicated triggers
- “Is data isolation a requirement, or is it mostly about predictable throughput?”
- “Do you anticipate needing reserved capacity for peak events?”
- “Any concerns about noisy neighbors or quota predictability?”

Private/VPC triggers
- “Do you have a hard requirement for customer-managed networking (VPC), on-prem, or air-gapped?”
- “Any compliance frameworks driving the decision (SOC2, HIPAA, ISO, PCI)?”
- “Do you need customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?”
- “What are your retention requirements for logs/prompts/outputs?”

SSO/RBAC/audit
- “Do you need SSO/SAML from day one?”
- “Who needs access (admins vs read-only)? Do you need RBAC by project/team?”
- “Do you require audit logs for key actions (key creation, policy changes, model pin updates)?”

Data handling clarity questions (avoid surprises later)
- “Can any prompts/outputs contain PII/PHI? If yes, what’s your redaction/encryption expectation?”
- “Do you need data residency guarantees for inference + logs?”

8) Decision process + procurement (don’t skip)
Goal: qualify timeline and next steps; uncover blockers.

Questions
- “What triggered this evaluation and what’s the deadline?”
- “Who signs off—engineering, security, procurement, finance? Anyone not on the call?”
- “Is this replacing an existing vendor or enabling a net-new feature?”
- “What’s the budget model you prefer: usage-based, reserved capacity, or hybrid?”
- “Any legal requirements we should anticipate (DPA, security questionnaire, pen test, SLA terms)?”

Next-step / mutual action plan prompts
- “If today goes well, what’s the next milestone? (POC kickoff, security review, architecture review)”
- “What would you need to see in a POC to feel confident?”

9) Quick “choose the demo path” mapping (internal cheat)
If they say… → show…
- “We need fast integration + streaming UI” → Core API streaming + SDK snippet + retries
- “We need JSON outputs to drive workflows” → Structured output + tool calling example
- “Costs are climbing / CFO watching” → Token-level cost breakdown + caching/batching toggles + before/after comparison
- “We had outages / rate limits hurt us” → Fallback routing policy + graceful degradation story + health/alerts (narrative)
- “We can’t operate another black box” → Console dashboards + traces + error analysis + rollouts
- “Security will block hosted” → Private/VPC architecture narrative + audit logs + SSO/RBAC (mostly narrative + screenshots)

10) Objection-handling discovery prompts (ask before you defend)
- “When you say ‘latency is too high,’ where is it high—first token, total time, tail latency, or under concurrency?”
- “When you say ‘cost,’ is it per-token rate, prompt length, retries, or infra overhead?”
- “When you say ‘private,’ is it about network path, key management, compliance scope, or internal policy?”
- “If we could guarantee predictable throughput, would hosted be acceptable, or is VPC a hard requirement regardless?”
- “What would make you confident we won’t regress quality after a model change?”

11) Notes template (copy/paste into HubSpot)
- Use case:
- Workload type (chat/embeddings/rerank):
- Latency targets (P50/P95):
- Throughput/QPS (avg/peak):
- Context length / tokens (avg/max):
- Key constraints (residency, retention, PII/PHI):
- Preferred deployment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) + why:
- Must-have features (tools, JSON, streaming, evals, rollouts):
- Current solution + pain:
- Stakeholders + decision maker:
- Timeline + next step:

12) Small but important reminders (internal)
- Don’t over-commit on specific model availability; talk in terms of pinned versions + compatible fallbacks.
- If they ask about security artifacts: offer the demo security FAQ links and propose a dedicated security review call.
- If procurement appears early: steer to value + success criteria, then align on pricing model (usage vs reserved) and next steps.

Appendix A: ultra-short question sets by demo length

20-minute exec demo (pick 3 questions total)
- “What’s the customer-facing feature and what does ‘success’ look like?”
- “Is the main pain cost, latency, or reliability?”
- “Any non-negotiables: VPC/private, residency, SSO?”

30-minute standard demo (recommended)
- Use case/workload shape (2)
- Priority: cost vs latency vs predictability (1)
- Deployment/security constraint (1)
- Decision process/timeline (1)

60-minute technical deep dive
- Add: rollouts/evals approach, tracing integration, fallback policy preferences, token distributions, and POC success metrics
